test_title: PYST 34: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 28 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Constitutional provisions can be amended by an ordinary Act of Parliament (simple majority), rather than through the special procedure under Article 368?

options.text: Article 2 (Parliament may by law admit new states)

solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 2** of the Constitution of India provides **Parliament the power to admit new states into the Union of India** or establish new states.
 
• This article grants Parliament the authority to enact laws for the creation or admission of states through a **simple majority**, not requiring the special amendment process under **Article 368**.
 
• The provision under Article 2 is utilized when India integrates new territories or regions. For example, **Sikkim** was admitted as a state of India in **1975** under this article. *Hence, Article 2 can be amended by an ordinary Act of Parliament. Statement 1 is correct.*
 
• **Article 356** and **Article 368** require constitutional processes and cannot be amended by a simple majority. These provisions are subject to stricter conditions. *Hence, Article 356 and Article 368 cannot be amended by an ordinary Act of Parliament. Statement 2 and 3 are incorrect.*
 
• **Article 14**, which guarantees equality before the law, is a fundamental right enshrined in Part III of the Constitution. It cannot be amended by a simple Act of Parliament as it forms part of the basic structure of the Constitution. *Statement 4 is also incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 2 of the Constitution:**

 
 
• Article 2 grants Parliament the authority to admit new states or establish new states within the Union of India.
 
• It is a procedural article allowing the expansion of India's territorial boundaries through legislative action.
 
• Examples include the integration of **Sikkim** and creation of new states such as **Telangana** through reorganization.
 
 
 
• **Article 356:**
 
 
• This article empowers the President to impose **President’s Rule** in a state under certain circumstances.
 
• It requires specific legal and constitutional grounds, such as the breakdown of constitutional machinery in the state.
 
• It cannot be amended through a simple majority, as it forms a critical aspect of the federal structure.
 
 
 
• **Article 368:**
 
 
• Article 368 provides the procedure for amending the Constitution.
 
• It outlines a **special procedure** requiring a two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament and ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.
 
• Hence, amendments to fundamental provisions cannot be done via a simple majority.
 
 
 
• **Article 14:**
 
 
• Article 14 guarantees **equality before law** and equal protection of the laws to all individuals within the territory of India.
 
• It is a fundamental right forming part of the **basic structure of the Constitution**.
 
• Any amendment or change to this article requires the special procedure outlined in Article 368.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Provisions for Constitutional Amendments:**

 
 
• Constitutional provisions are categorized into two types for amendments: those amendable by a **simple majority** and those requiring the **special procedure** under Article 368.
 
• Provisions related to the organization of states, such as Articles 2 and 3, can be amended via a simple majority.
 
• Fundamental rights and structural provisions, such as Articles 14, 368, and others, require a special procedure for amendment.
 
• The basic structure doctrine, established in the **Keshavananda Bharati case (1973)**, ensures that certain provisions cannot be altered.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Reorganization:**
 
 
• Reorganization of states has been carried out under Articles 2 and 3, such as the formation of **Chhattisgarh** (2000), **Uttarakhand** (2000), and **Telangana** (2014).
 
• Such reorganizations are based on socio-political considerations, linguistic factors, or administrative needs.
